Summary: Adam's Eden task: to dress and keep the garden God planted.
Commandment: Dress and keep the garden of Eden.
Application: Work precedes the Fall in this account: tending is part of humanity's original calling, not a curse. The specific garden task ended with the expulsion (Genesis 3:23-24); the work ethic it embodies is carried elsewhere, but this row covers the Eden task itself, not work in general.
Purpose: To tend the garden God planted as humanity's first appointed work; the task belongs to Eden and ended when Adam and Eve were sent out.
Function: Work precedes the Fall in this account: tending is part of humanity's original calling, not a curse. This command predates Sinai, so the civil, ceremonial, and moral division does not sort it. Its goal was to tend the garden God planted — to dress and keep it, as humanity's first appointed work. The evil or restraint angle does not apply here; no particular evil is named, only a task given. The specific garden task ended with the expulsion, though the work ethic it embodies is carried elsewhere in Scripture.
